examples.ko: 이 가게는 직접 만든 수공품만 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop only sells handmade items.
Since they're handmade, no two look the same.
I bought a pretty handmade cup at the market.
Handmade goods are more expensive than machine-made ones.

examples.ko: 외국 친구에게 줄 수공품을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a handmade gift for my foreign friend.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들이 직접 만든 수공품이에요.
examples.en: These are handicrafts made by the people of this village.

explain: '공예품'은 예술적인 솜씨가 들어간 물건을 말할 때 잘 어울리고, '수공품'은 기계가 아니라 손으로 만들었다는 점을 강조해요. 요즘은 '핸드메이드'라는 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '공예품' (craft) fits objects with artistic skill, while '수공품' stresses that something was made by hand, not by machine. People also say '핸드메이드' (handmade) these days.

examples.en: The kids were whispering at the back of the classroom.

examples.ko: 사람들이 나를 보며 수군대는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like people are whispering while looking at me.
Don't whisper behind my back, say it to me directly.

examples.ko: 둘이 귀에 대고 뭔가를 수군대고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are whispering something into each other's ears.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들이 그 소문을 두고 수군대요.
examples.en: People at the company are whispering about that rumor.
When I walked in, the staff started whispering.

explain: '수군거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 여럿이 작은 소리로 남의 이야기를 하는 느낌이 강해요. 다정하게 말하는 '속삭이다'와 달리 소문이나 험담처럼 부정적인 장면에 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the same as '수군거리다' and suggests several people talking quietly about someone else. Unlike the gentler '속삭이다' (to whisper), it often fits negative scenes such as rumors or gossip.

examples.en: The kids are gathered together talking in whispers.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 수군수군 얘기하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear someone whispering behind me.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 수군수군 비밀 이야기를 나눠요.
examples.en: The two of them share secrets in whispers.
In the library, even whispers can be heard by everyone.
My friends were whispering and laughing next to me.

examples.ko: 수군수군 말하지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't whisper, speak up.

explain: '속닥속닥'처럼 작은 소리로 말하는 모양을 나타내는데, 여러 사람이 남 이야기를 하는 느낌이 있어요. 동사로는 '수군대다'를 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Like '속닥속닥', it describes talking in low voices, but it often suggests several people talking about someone else. The matching verb is '수군대다'.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 낮의 더위가 조금 수그러들었어요.
examples.en: When the rain came, the daytime heat eased a little.
As time passed, my anger died down a bit.
That controversy isn't dying down easily.
Once the wind dies down, the boat will leave.
Let's wait until the trend dies down.
My fever has gone down, so I'm okay now.

explain: 기세, 열, 화, 논란, 더위처럼 강하던 것이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '가라앉다'보다 '세던 것이 꺾인다'는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when something strong, such as momentum, fever, anger, controversy or heat, gradually weakens. Compared with '가라앉다', it feels more like something forceful losing its edge.

examples.ko: 시간이 지나니 흥분이 수그러진 것 같아요.
examples.en: As time passed, the excitement seems to have settled.
His fervor is gradually fading.

examples.ko: 비가 그치니 바람도 수그러지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Now that the rain stopped, the wind seems to be dying down too.
When I got praised, my head bowed on its own.
His voice faded and soon it went quiet.
Let's talk again when your anger has cooled down.

explain: '수그리다'의 피동 느낌으로, 고개가 숙여지거나 기세·화·흥분이 약해질 때 써요. 기세가 약해지는 뜻은 '수그러들다'와 거의 비슷해요.
explain_en: It works like a passive of '수그리다': a head gets lowered, or momentum, anger or excitement weakens. In the sense of weakening, it is very close to '수그러들다'.

examples.en: I greeted them with my head slightly bowed.
He lowered his head out of embarrassment.
I bent over and picked up the coin from the floor.
The ceiling is low, so you have to duck.
Why do you keep lowering your head?

examples.ko: 그는 고개를 수그린 채 말없이 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat silently with his head bowed.

explain: '숙이다'와 같은 뜻으로 고개, 허리, 몸 앞에 써요. 반대로 고개를 드는 건 '들다'나 '치켜들다'라고 하고, 저절로 숙여지는 건 '수그러지다'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '숙이다' and goes with head, waist or body. The opposite is '고개를 들다' (raise your head), and when something lowers on its own you say '수그러지다'.

examples.en: My aunt has an easygoing, gentle personality.
He's so easygoing that he gets along with anyone.
His clothes and the way he talked were both unpretentious.
The way he smiled so unpretentiously looked comfortable.
The landlord was so easygoing that I felt relieved.

examples.ko: 수더분하지만 할 말은 다 하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He's easygoing, but he still says what needs to be said.

explain: '털털하다'와 비슷하게 꾸밈없고 까다롭지 않은 사람을 좋게 말할 때 써요. 반대로 까다롭고 예민한 사람은 '까다롭다'나 '예민하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Like '털털하다', it describes a person who is unpretentious and not fussy, in a good way. The opposite types are called '까다롭다' (picky) or '예민하다' (sensitive).

examples.en: He is a monk who lives in a mountain temple.
The monk wakes up every dawn to pray.

examples.ko: 영화에서 본 수도승의 삶이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The life of the monk I saw in the movie was impressive.
I want to live quietly like a monk.
The monks are eating in silence.
He left his family to become a monk.

explain: 불교의 승려는 보통 '스님'이라고 불러요. '수도승'은 수도하며 사는 사람을 두루 가리키고, '수도사'라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: Buddhist monks are usually called '스님'. '수도승' refers broadly to people living a life of religious training, and '수도사' is another word for this.

examples.en: This coffee grinder is the manual type.
It's a manual door, so you have to push it by hand.

examples.ko: 전기가 나가도 수동식 펌프는 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even when the power goes out, you can use a manual pump.

examples.ko: 수동식과 자동식 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which is better, manual or automatic?
These days manual washing machines are hard to find.
If you switch to the manual type, it's much cheaper.

explain: 반대말은 '자동식'이에요. '수동'만 쓰면 '수동 모드'처럼 손으로 하는 방식을 말하고, 문법에서는 '수동태'처럼 '당하는 쪽'이라는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '자동식' (automatic type). '수동' alone, as in '수동 모드', means doing it by hand, and in grammar it also means 'passive', as in '수동태'.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 간 거실은 장난감으로 수라장이에요.
examples.en: The living room is a mess of toys after the kids played.

examples.ko: 새벽부터 줄을 선 사람들이 한꺼번에 밀려서 매장 앞이 수라장이 됐어요.
examples.en: The people lined up since dawn all surged forward at once, and the front of the store turned into chaos.
Right after the accident, the scene was sheer chaos.

examples.ko: 시험 전날이면 내 방은 수라장이 따로 없어요.
examples.en: The day before an exam, my room is nothing short of chaos.

examples.ko: 갑자기 불이 꺼지자 극장 안이 수라장으로 변했어요.
examples.en: When the lights suddenly went out, the theater turned into chaos.
You have to stay calm even in the middle of chaos.

explain: 보통은 '아수라장'이라고 많이 말하고, '수라장'은 같은 뜻의 줄인 모양이에요. 말투가 편한 자리에서는 '난장판'이나 '엉망진창'도 써요.
explain_en: People usually say '아수라장', and '수라장' is a shorter form with the same meaning. In casual talk you can also say '난장판' or '엉망진창'.

examples.en: The car got stuck in the mire and couldn't move.
After the rain, the road turned into a mire.
I want to escape from the quagmire of debt.
Once you fall into a quagmire, it's hard to get out.
The economy is sinking into a quagmire.

examples.ko: 이 늪은 수렁 같아서 발이 푹 빠져요.
examples.en: This swamp is like a bog, and your feet sink right in.

explain: 진흙이 깊어 발이 빠지는 곳이지만, 실제로는 빚, 불황, 절망처럼 헤어나기 힘든 상황을 비유할 때 더 자주 들려요. '늪'과 비슷하게 쓰는데 '수렁'은 빠져나오기 힘들다는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: The company sank into a long recession.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 진흙이 아니라, 빠져나오기 힘든 나쁜 상황에 놓였다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not real mud: it figuratively means being stuck in a bad situation that is hard to escape.

explain_en: It is literally deep mud that swallows your feet, but it is often heard as a metaphor for situations that are hard to escape, such as debt, recession or despair. It is close to '늪' (swamp), with a strong sense of being unable to get out.

examples.en: I went to a training center during this vacation.
The school's training center is near a mountain.
I had a campfire with my friends at the training center.

examples.ko: 가족 단위로도 이 수련원을 예약할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also book this training center as a family.
The training center program was more fun than I expected.
The new employees left for training at the training center.

explain: 학교나 단체가 합숙 활동을 하러 가는 시설이에요. 그 행사는 '수련회'라고 하고, 회사 교육 시설은 '연수원'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a facility where schools or groups go for overnight activities. The event itself is called '수련회', and company training facilities are also called '연수원'.

examples.ko: 마침 일요일이라 수련의들은 휴일도 반납하고 달려왔어요.
examples.en: It happened to be Sunday, but the interns gave up their day off and rushed in.
Doctors in training learn a lot from senior doctors.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 병원에서 수련의로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm currently working at the hospital as a resident.
The resident stayed by the patient's side all night.

examples.ko: 수련의 시절에는 잠을 거의 못 잤어요.
examples.en: During my residency, I barely slept.
I asked the resident my questions.

explain: 의사 면허를 딴 뒤 병원에서 전문 과정을 밟는 의사를 말해요. 일상에서는 '인턴', '레지던트'라는 말도 많이 쓰고, 공식적인 이름은 '전공의'예요.
explain_en: It refers to a licensed doctor undergoing specialist training at a hospital. In daily talk people also say '인턴' and '레지던트', and the official term is '전공의'.

examples.en: How much did you actually receive this month?
After taxes, the amount you receive drops a lot too.

examples.ko: 보험금 수령액을 미리 계산해 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can calculate the insurance payout in advance.
Check just the amount of salary you receive separately.
Your lifestyle changes depending on the pension you receive.
You get a text message when the amount is deposited.

explain: 받는 사람 입장에서 말하는 금액이에요. 주는 쪽에서는 '지급액'이라고 하고, 일상 대화에서는 '받는 돈'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the amount from the receiver's point of view. The paying side calls it '지급액', and in casual talk people also say '받는 돈'.

en: person who has completed a course

examples.ko: 이번 과정의 수료자는 모두 서른 명이에요.
examples.en: There are thirty people in total who completed this course.
We give a certificate to those who complete the course.
The list of completers was posted on the bulletin board.

examples.ko: 교육 수료자만 다음 단계에 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only those who completed the training can apply for the next level.

examples.ko: 저도 작년에 이 과정의 수료자가 됐어요.
examples.en: I also completed this course last year.
The completers gathered to take a commemorative photo.

explain: '졸업자'는 학교를 마치고 졸업장을 받은 사람이고, '수료자'는 강좌나 과정을 끝낸 사람이에요. 그래서 학위가 아니라 '수료증'을 받는 경우에 어울려요.
explain_en: A '졸업자' finished a school and got a diploma, while a '수료자' finished a course or program. That is why it fits cases where you receive a '수료증' (completion certificate) rather than a degree.

examples.en: The government buys rice from farmers.

examples.ko: 올해는 가격이 올라서 더 많이 수매했어요.
examples.en: Prices went up this year, so they bought more.

examples.ko: 마을 조합이 감자를 모두 수매하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The village cooperative decided to buy all the potatoes.
The rice that was purchased is stored in a warehouse.

examples.ko: 농협이 값을 정해서 사과를 수매할 거예요.
examples.en: The agricultural cooperative will set a price and buy the apples.
The price at which the government buys changes every year.

explain: 그냥 '사다'가 아니라 정부나 조합 같은 기관이 농산물 등을 생산자에게서 사들일 때 써요. '수매 가격', '수매량'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is not just 'to buy': it is used when an institution such as the government or a cooperative buys farm products from producers. It also appears as a noun in '수매 가격' and '수매량'.

examples.ko: 이 집은 수맥 위에 있어서 잠이 안 온대요.
examples.en: They say this house sits on a water vein, so you can't sleep.

examples.ko: 우물을 팔 곳을 정하려고 수맥부터 알아봐요.
examples.en: To decide where to dig a well, we check the water vein first.

examples.ko: 땅속 수맥이 막혀서 물이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The underground water vein is blocked, so no water comes out.
I called an expert who surveys water veins.

examples.ko: 수맥으로 물이 흘러서 땅이 늘 촉촉해요.
examples.en: Water flows through the vein, so the ground is always damp.
I moved the bed far away from the water vein.

explain: 땅속에서 물이 흐르는 줄기를 말하고, 우물을 팔 때 중요해요. 민간에서는 집터나 잠자리에 수맥이 있으면 좋지 않다는 이야기도 하지만, 일반적인 말은 '지하수'예요.
explain_en: It is a stream of water flowing underground, important when digging a well. Folk belief also says a water vein under a house or bed is bad, but the general word for groundwater is '지하수'.

examples.en: This painting is an ink wash painting drawn only with ink.
I saw an old ink wash painting at the museum.
The spreading feel of the ink in ink wash painting is beautiful.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 취미로 수묵화에 푹 빠져 계세요.
examples.en: My grandfather is deeply into ink wash painting as a hobby.
Do you want to go to an ink wash painting exhibition together?

examples.ko: 산과 물을 그린 수묵화가 거실에 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: An ink wash painting of mountains and water hangs in the living room.

explain: 먹의 진하고 옅은 정도로 그리는 동양화를 말해요. 넓은 말은 '동양화'나 '한국화'이고, 서양식 물감 그림은 '서양화'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is an East Asian painting made with darker and lighter shades of ink. The broader terms are '동양화' and '한국화', and Western-style paint pictures are called '서양화'.

examples.en: I watched the gate guard changing ceremony in front of the palace.
In the old days, the gate guard opened and closed the castle gate.
The gate guard's costume was really colorful.
Tourists take photos with the gate guard.
Our team's goalkeeper is a reliable guardian of the goal.
I asked the gate guard for directions.

explain: 조선 시대에 궁궐이나 성문을 지키던 관리를 말해요. 지금은 경복궁 같은 곳의 '수문장 교대식'이 유명하고, 스포츠 기사에서는 골키퍼를 '골문을 지키는 수문장'이라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It was the officer who guarded palace or castle gates in the Joseon era. Today the 'gate guard changing ceremony' at places like Gyeongbokgung is well known, and sports articles sometimes call a goalkeeper the '수문장' of the goal.

examples.en: They piled rice high on the plate for me.
I walked along a road deep with piled-up snow.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 쓰레기가 수북수북 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Garbage is piled high in front of the house.
I heaped tangerines into the basket.
The park with heaps of fallen leaves is pretty.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 서류가 수북수북 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Documents are piled high on the desk.

explain: '수북'을 되풀이한 말로, 소복하게 쌓인 모습을 더 생생하게 나타내요. 눈, 낙엽, 음식, 서류처럼 쌓이는 것에 어울려요.
explain_en: It repeats '수북' and describes things piled up in heaps in a more vivid way. It suits things that pile up, such as snow, leaves, food or documents.

examples.en: They piled rice high on my plate.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 온 집의 창가에 먼지가 수북이 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Dust had piled up on the windowsill since I hadn't been home in a while.
Fallen leaves lay piled in heaps across the yard.

examples.ko: 배가 고파서 밥을 수북이 퍼서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was hungry, so I scooped a heaping portion of rice and ate it.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 서류가 수북이 쌓인 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw documents piled high on the desk.

examples.ko: 눈이 수북이 쌓여서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: Snow has piled up deep, so cars can't get through.

explain: '수북하다'의 부사형이에요. '가득'은 그릇이 꽉 찬 것이고, '수북이'는 그릇 위로 솟아오를 만큼 쌓인 모양이에요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '수북하다'. '가득' means filled to the brim, while '수북이' means piled up so high it rises above the rim.

examples.en: The child's rice bowl is always heaped full.
Dust lay thick on the desk.
It was hard shoveling the deeply piled snow.
I was given a plate heaped with food.

examples.ko: 음식이 너무 수북해서 뚜껑이 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: The food is piled so high that the lid won't close.
It's not heaped up, but there's plenty of rice.

explain: '가득하다'는 꽉 찬 것이고, '수북하다'는 위로 솟을 만큼 쌓인 모양이에요. '소복하다'는 눈처럼 더 얕고 포근하게 쌓인 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '가득하다' means full, while '수북하다' means piled up higher than the container. '소복하다' feels shallower and softer, as with a light layer of snow.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 수비력이 약해서 점수를 많이 내줘요.
examples.en: Our team's defense is weak, so we give up a lot of points.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌에는 수비력도 눈에 띄게 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: This season our defense has noticeably improved too.
When it comes to defense, our team is the best in the league.
The offense is good, but the defense is lacking.
We train every day to build up our defense.

examples.ko: 수비력에서는 상대 팀이 한 수 위예요.
examples.en: In defense, the opposing team is a step above.

explain: '공격력'과 짝을 이루는 말로, 주로 스포츠에서 막는 힘을 말해요. 막는 행동 자체는 '수비'라고 하고, 그 능력을 말할 때 '수비력'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '공격력' (offensive power) and mostly refers to the ability to defend in sports. The act of defending is '수비', and '수비력' is the ability to do it.

examples.en: Our team's defensive line is so shaky.
The defense wavered, and we conceded the first goal.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선수가 수비진에 큰 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: The newly arrived player is a big help to the defense.
The coach rearranged the defensive line.
The defenders and the goalkeeper work well together.
The defense also stayed focused throughout the match.

explain: '수비수'는 선수 한 명이고, '수비진'은 수비를 맡은 선수들 전체를 말해요. 공격을 맡은 쪽은 '공격진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A '수비수' is a single defender, while '수비진' is the whole group of players in charge of defense. The attacking group is called '공격진'.

examples.en: The police's investigative ability has improved a lot.

examples.ko: 이 사건은 수사력의 한계를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: This case showed the limits of investigative ability.
There was criticism that the police's investigative capacity is lacking.

examples.ko: 검찰은 모든 수사력을 모아 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The prosecution is investigating with all its investigative resources.

examples.ko: 수사력 강화를 위해 인원을 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to add staff to strengthen investigative capacity.
The team stronger in investigation took over the case.

explain: '수사력을 동원하다', '수사력이 부족하다'처럼 수사 기관이 가진 능력이나 인력을 말할 때 써요. 범죄를 밝히는 일은 경찰·검찰의 '수사'이고, 범죄가 아닌 일을 알아볼 때는 '조사'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for the ability or manpower of an investigating body, as in '수사력을 동원하다' (mobilize investigative resources) and '수사력이 부족하다' (lack investigative capacity). Looking into a crime is '수사' by police or prosecutors, while checking into non-criminal matters is '조사'.
